subject: Request: Temporary SLO adjustment & commercial concession for Velari Health pilot
messages:
From: Ethan Ramirez <ethan.ramirez@velarihealth.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Cc: Velari Health Procurement <procurement@velarihealth.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLO ask — latency & uptime thresholds

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Velari is excited to pilot Redwood as the inference layer for our clinical triage product. Before we lock dates, Procurement asked that we document two things so our security and ops teams can sign off: a temporary SLO adjustment for the pilot period and confirmation of the commercial offset.

Specifically:
- Pilot duration: 60 days (staging -> limited prod).
- Requested uptime tolerance for pilot: 99.0% (we understand production SLAs are higher).
- Latency: P99 tail target of <= 950ms for the inference route (our UX tolerates brief spikes but P99 matters).
- Service credits: we asked for an explicit cap (we proposed a $5k aggregate cap for pilot disruptions).
- Commercial ask: a pilot discount of 15% on list pricing for the 60-day pilot.

Attached is our internal note with failure-mode expectations and the procurement checklist. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accommodate a temporary SLO carveout plus the pilot discount, and what the approval path looks like?

Attachments: [Attachment: velari_sla_requirements.pdf (PDF)]

Thanks,
Ethan Ramirez
Director, Platform Ops — Velari Health
procurement@velarihealth.com

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Ramirez <ethan.ramirez@velarihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask — latency & uptime thresholds

Ethan — thanks for the clear ask and the attachment. Looping in Marissa from Deal Desk to scope the commercial side.

Summary of what we heard: 60-day pilot, desire for 99.0% uptime tolerance, P99 <= 950ms, $5k cap on credits, and a 15% pilot discount.

From an initial ops standpoint: we can operate a pilot with a temporary SLO variance, but we typically limit pilot uptime deviations to 30–90 days and set a single aggregate credit cap. We also need to ensure routing and capacity isolation so other customers are unaffected.

Marissa — can Deal Desk consider a pilot concession along these lines? My recommendation to accelerate timelines is: offer a commercial package now that gives Velari visibility (discount + defined credit cap + documented remediation plan) and take Exec signoff for any discount above 10% or SLO variance longer than 45 days.

If we can agree to a single offer quickly I can send a redlined offer and DocuSign to their procurement team.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Pilot SLO ask — commercial proposal

Chloe / Ben — read the ask. My suggested commercial guardrails to keep risk acceptable but win the pilot quickly:

Proposed package (Deal Desk recommendation):
- Pilot length: 60 days (start date to be confirmed).
- Temporary uptime tolerance: 99.1% for the 60-day pilot (a middle ground vs their 99.0%).
- Latency commitment: P99 <= 1.0s for the pilot route; we will include a one-way SLA for this route only (monitoring hooks + alerting).
- Service credits: explicit aggregate cap of $5,000 for the pilot, payable as a one-time credit on the first post-pilot invoice if thresholds missed. No recurring credits.
- Discount: 12% off list for the pilot period. Anything >10% needs Exec signoff; recommending 12% to close.
- Legal: require a short addendum limiting remedy to the pilot window and excluding indemnity changes.

Risks/notes:
- Larger discount or longer SLO variance increases commercial exposure and precedent risk.
- Engineering will need tagging/routing to enforce pilot isolation; Ops signoff required (I can coordinate).

If Ben signs off we can proceed to Exec approval for the 12% and SLO deviation (since this is both a price concession and a terms deviation). I can draft the addendum and offer.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head, Deal Desk — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO ask — Exec approval needed

Marissa / Chloe — I reviewed the proposal. I support a constrained concession to secure the pilot but want one tweak for risk control.

Approval & conditions:
- Approve 12% pilot discount and the temporary SLO deviation to 99.1% for 60 days.
- Service credits: cap at $5,000 aggregate for the pilot as proposed.
- Require Legal to prepare a brief addendum that: (1) explicitly limits remedies to the single pilot period; (2) requires Velari to raise production concerns within 30 days of pilot end for any credit eligibility; (3) includes a maximum liability carveout aligned with our standard pilot terms.
- Commercial signoff is contingent on Legal & Compliance confirming no data residency or audit conflicts.

Marissa — once Legal confirms the addendum I authorize Deal Desk to finalize the offer and send to Velari with DocuSign.

Ben Carter
VP, Commercials — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
